document.title: Memorandum of Conversation between Secretary Baker and Eduard Shevardnadze, March 20, 1990
document.authors: U.S. Department of State (Mandatory Review M-2017-16468)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Soviet Withdrawal from Afghanistan 1989 | National Security Archive
document.note: In Namibia, Baker and Shevardnadze seek a solution on Afghanistan. The US demands Najibullah go and not stand in elections; Shevardnadze argues for UN-monitored free elections. He says no Mujahedin leader will accept free elections: 'They all have a dictatorial persuasion—Hekmatiyar, Khalis—you name it.'

mentions.quote: My feeling is that we ought to try to do the same thing in Afghanistan.
One year ago I visited Kabul and the city was being shelled all the time

Hekmatiyar, Khalis -- you name it; they are not interested in elections.

events.description: Baker and Shevardnadze meet in Windhoek and discuss Afghanistan elections, Najib, ceasefire and negative symmetry.
Failed coup attempt against Najib led by the defense minister with Khalq-wing generals; he fled to Pakistan.
Shevardnadze visits Kabul while city shelled and meets Najib and his wife.
Baker and Shevardnadze discuss Afghanistan, Najibullah, free elections and Mujahideen intransigence, then South Africa reform.
Shevardnadze visited Kabul during shelling and met Najibullah and his family; Najibullah's wife declined to go to Moscow.
Baker met Pik Botha in Rome, who outlined a platform of dismantling apartheid.
Baker-Shevardnadze meeting in Windhoek, covering open skies, summit timing, German unification, and Afghanistan.
Proposed Bush-Gorbachev summit (June 11-15 or June 18-22), ending at Kennebunkport.
Failed coup attempt against Najibullah led by the defense minister with Khalq-wing generals; he fled to Pakistan.
Shevardnadze visited shelled Kabul and met Najib and his family.
Baker proposes elections, ceasefire and negative symmetry if Najib is not in power; Shevardnadze rejects Najib's departure.

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze admits USSR pays salary and provides weapons to Najib.
relationships.quote: we don't just pay his salary, it is more broad than that. But yes, we do provide him weapons.

relationships.detail: Defense minister led coup against Najib and fled to Pakistan.
relationships.quote: he is now in Pakistan and Najibullah is still in Kabul

relationships.detail: Defense minister represented Khalq wing.
relationships.quote: representing the Khalq wing of the party

relationships.detail: Najib is leader of PDPA government.
relationships.quote: There could even be a PDPA candidate in that first election.

relationships.detail: Named among Mujahideen leaders.
relationships.quote: Not one leader of the Mujahaddin is going to accept free elections... Hekmatiyar, Khalis

relationships.detail: Named among Mujahideen leaders.
relationships.quote: Hekmatiyar, Khalis -- you name it

relationships.detail: Visited Kabul and spent time with Najib and family during shelling.
relationships.quote: I spent some time with Najib and his family

relationships.detail: Meeting in Windhoek.
relationships.quote: PARTICIPANTS: Secretary Baker Eduard Shevardnadze

relationships.detail: Baker proposed that Najibullah abide by election results but not run in the first election; Shevardnadze was skeptical.
relationships.quote: have him agree that he would not run in the first election, but he would be eligible for any election after that.

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze visited Kabul a year earlier during shelling and spent time with Najibullah and his family.
relationships.quote: One year ago I visited Kabul and the city was being shelled all the time

relationships.detail: Najibullah is implicitly linked to the PDPA, which Baker suggests could field a candidate in a first election.
relationships.quote: There could even be a PDPA candidate in that first election.

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze names Hekmatyar among Mujahideen leaders who oppose free elections.
relationships.quote: Not one leader of the Mujahaddin is going to accept free elections. They all have a dictatorial pérsuasion -- Hekmatiyar, Khalis

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze names Khalis among Mujahideen leaders who oppose free elections.
relationships.quote: Not one leader of the Mujahaddin is going to accept free elections.

relationships.detail: The Mujahideen refuse elections while Najibullah remains in power.
relationships.quote: how can we have an election if Najib is not going to go?

relationships.detail: Baker met Pik Botha in Rome a year earlier, when Botha described plans to dismantle apartheid.
relationships.quote: A year ago I met Pik Botha in Rome and he told me they were going to run on a platform of ending white domination.

relationships.detail: Baker passed proposed summit dates to the Soviets through Ambassador Matlock.
relationships.quote: I gave you some dates through Ambassador Matlock and those dates of June 18-22

relationships.detail: Bush wished to host Gorbachev at his Kennebunkport home in Maine during the planned summit.
relationships.quote: President Bush would then like it if President Gorbachev could come up to his home in Maine at Kennebunkport

relationships.detail: Bush's home is at Kennebunkport, Maine.
relationships.quote: his home in Maine at Kennebunkport

relationships.detail: Najibullah remains in power in Kabul.
relationships.quote: So he is now in Pakistan and Najibullah is still in Kabul.

relationships.detail: The defense minister led a coup attempt with generals against Najib.
relationships.quote: someone who was the defense minister who had all the generals with him fighting against Najib representing the Khalq wing of the party

relationships.detail: The defense minister represented the Khalq wing.
relationships.quote: representing the Khalq wing of the party

relationships.detail: After the failed coup the defense minister is now in Pakistan.
relationships.quote: So he is now in Pakistan

relationships.detail: Shevardnadze says the USSR always had good relations with the Khalq wing.
relationships.quote: we always had good relations with that wing of the party

relationships.detail: The Soviets pay Najib's salary more broadly and provide weapons.
relationships.quote: we don't just pay his salary, it is more broad than that. But yes, we do provide him weapons.

relationships.detail: Najib proposed free elections under UN auspices.
relationships.quote: He is saying they can be held under UN auspices

relationships.detail: Baker refers to telling the Paks, Saudis and Mujahideen that Najib will leave.
relationships.quote: if we could tell the Paks, the Saudis, and the Mujahaddin that at some point he is not going to be there

relationships.detail: Saudis grouped with the Paks and Mujahideen as US-aligned parties.
relationships.quote: tell the Paks, the Saudis, and the Mujahaddin

key_claims: Baker states the US cannot produce Mujahideen participation in a political process while Najib remains in power.
Baker proposes that Najib not run in the first election but be eligible later.
Shevardnadze says the USSR continues to supply Najib with weapons and salary.
Shevardnadze argues Najib survived a Khalq-led coup attempt and has strengthened his position.
Shevardnadze asserts no Mujahideen leader, including Hekmatyar and Khalis, would accept free elections.
Baker suggests telling Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and the Mujahideen that Najib will eventually leave.
